questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Electrophilic aromatic substitution on pyrrole, furan, and thiophene occurs predominantly at which ring position?
questions.explanationEn: Attack of an electrophile at **C2 ($\alpha$-position)** generates a carbocation intermediate stabilized by **three** resonance structures, whereas attack at C3 ($\beta$-position) yields only **two** resonance structures. Hence, C2-substitution is strongly favored. Option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which naturally occurring L-$\alpha$-amino acid possesses an $(R)$ absolute configuration at its $\alpha$-carbon according to Cahn–Ingold–Prelog (CIP) rules?
questions.explanationEn: In 18 of the 19 chiral proteinogenic L-amino acids, the priority order is $-\text{NH}_2 > -\text{CO}_2\text{H} > -\text{R} > -\text{H}$, giving the $(S)$ configuration. In **L-cysteine**, the side chain $-\text{CH}_2\text{SH}$ contains sulfur ($Z = 16$), which outranks $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ (bonded to oxygen, $Z = 8$). Swapping priorities 2 and 3 reverses the CIP label to **$(R)$**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: A **nucleoside** consists of a nitrogenous base covalently attached to
optionsEn: a pentose sugar only (without a phosphate group)
a pentose sugar and one phosphate group
a hexose sugar and three phosphate groups
questions.explanationEn: A **nucleoside** is composed of a purine or pyrimidine base linked via an $N$-glycosidic bond to a pentose sugar (ribose or $2'$-deoxyribose). Adding one or more phosphate groups converts a nucleoside into a **nucleotide**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The reagent used in the **Edman degradation** to selectively cleave and identify the $N$-terminal amino acid residue of a peptide as a phenylthiohydantoin (PTH) derivative without hydrolyzing the remaining peptide chain is
questions.explanationEn: **Edman degradation** uses **phenyl isothiocyanate (PITC, $\text{PhN}=\text{C}=\text{S}$)** under mildly basic conditions followed by anhydrous acid ($\text{CF}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) to cleave only the $N$-terminal residue as a PTH derivative while leaving the rest of the peptide intact for iterative sequencing. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Oxidation of D-glucose with mild bromine water ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) selectively yields
questions.explanationEn: Bromine water ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is a mild oxidant that selectively oxidizes the C1 aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$) of an aldose to a carboxylic acid ($-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) without oxidizing the C6 primary alcohol, converting D-glucose into **D-gluconic acid** (an aldonic acid). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Kolbe–Schmitt reaction**, heating sodium phenoxide with $\text{CO}_2$ under pressure ($125\,^\circ\text{C}$, $4\text{--}7\text{ atm}$) followed by acidification gives predominantly **salicylic acid** (2-hydroxybenzoic acid), whereas using potassium phenoxide at higher temperature favors **4-hydroxybenzoic acid**. The *ortho*-selectivity with sodium phenoxide is primarily attributed to
optionsEn: chelation of the small $\text{Na}^+$ cation simultaneously to the phenoxide oxygen and the incoming $\text{CO}_2$ molecule, delivering $\text{CO}_2$ to the *ortho* position
complete steric blockade of the *para* position by $\text{Na}^+$
rearrangement of phenyl carbonate via a Fries pathway
questions.explanationEn: The small, strongly coordinating $\text{Na}^+$ ion forms a tight six-membered chelated transition state bridging the phenoxide oxygen and $\text{CO}_2$, selectively directing carboxylation to the ***ortho* position** to yield sodium salicylate. The larger, less tightly chelating $\text{K}^+$ ion allows attack at the less hindered *para* position. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In the **Lobry de Bruyn–Alberda van Ekenstein transformation**, treating D-glucose with dilute aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ yields an equilibrium mixture containing D-glucose, D-mannose, and D-fructose via a common
questions.explanationEn: Base abstracts the acidic C2 proton of open-chain D-glucose to form a planar **1,2-enediolate** intermediate. Reprotonation at C2 from either face gives **D-glucose** and its C2-epimer **D-mannose**, while tautomerization via protonation at C1 gives the 2-ketose **D-fructose**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Nitration of aniline directly with a mixture of concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ yields a surprisingly large proportion ($\sim 47\%$) of *m*-nitroaniline because
optionsEn: in strongly acidic medium, aniline is extensively protonated to the anilinium ion ($\text{PhNH}_3^+$), which is strongly *meta*-directing
steric hindrance completely blocks both *ortho* and *para* positions
questions.explanationEn: In concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4/\text{HNO}_3$, basic aniline is largely protonated to the **anilinium cation ($-\text{NH}_3^+$)**, which lacks a lone pair and is strongly electron-withdrawing ($-I$) and ***meta*-directing**. To obtain *para*-nitroaniline cleanly, aniline is first protected as acetanilide ($-\text{NHCOCH}_3$). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The **Fischer indole synthesis** of 2-methylindole is carried out by heating the phenylhydrazone of which carbonyl compound with an acid catalyst (such as $\text{ZnCl}_2$ or polyphosphoric acid)?
questions.explanationEn: In the **Fischer indole synthesis**, an arylhydrazone tautomerizes to an ene-hydrazine, undergoes a $[3,3]$-sigmatropic rearrangement, cyclizes, and eliminates $\text{NH}_3$. Using **acetone phenylhydrazone** ($\text{PhNHN}=\text{C(CH}_3)_2$) places one methyl group at **C2** and a hydrogen at C3, yielding **2-methylindole** (whereas propanal phenylhydrazone gives 3-methylindole/skatole). Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: In classical structure elucidation of the hemlock alkaloid **coniine** ($2$-propylpiperidine, $\text{C}_8\text{H}_{17}\text{N}$), dehydrogenation over zinc dust or $\text{Pd/C}$ yields **conyrine** ($2$-propylpyridine), whose oxidation with $\text{KMnO}_4$ affords
questions.explanationEn: Permanganate oxidation of an alkylpyridine oxidizes the entire alkyl side chain at C2 down to a $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group. Thus, $2$-propylpyridine (conyrine) oxidizes to **pyridine-2-carboxylic acid (picolinic acid)**, establishing the C2 attachment of the propyl chain in coniine. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **citral** (3,7-dimethylocta-2,6-dienal) and **myrcene** (7-methyl-3-methyleneocta-1,6-diene) is/are correct?
optionsEn: Both citral and myrcene obey the head-to-tail isoprene rule.
Reduction of citral with $\text{NaBH}_4$ in methanol yields the primary allylic alcohol geraniol/nerol.
Heating citral with aqueous $\text{K}_2\text{CO}_3$ triggers a retro-aldol cleavage yielding 6-methylhept-5-en-2-one and acetaldehyde.
Myrcene contains two stereogenic carbon centers.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Both have the classic head-to-tail 2,6-dimethyloctane monoterpene backbone.
- **(B) Correct:** $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the aldehyde of $(E)$-citral (geranial) to geraniol and $(Z)$-citral (neral) to nerol.
- **(C) Correct:** Base-promoted hydration followed by retro-aldol cleavage of $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated citral yields 6-methylhept-5-en-2-one and acetaldehyde (classical structure proof of citral).
- **(D) Incorrect:** Myrcene has **zero** chiral centers.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following aldohexoses yield an **optically inactive (*meso*) aldaric acid** upon oxidation with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$?
questions.explanationEn:
Oxidation with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ converts both C1 and C6 into $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups:
- **(A) D-Allose** (C2–C5 $\text{OH}$: R, R, R, R) $\to$ *meso*-allaric acid (horizontal plane of symmetry) $\implies$ optically inactive.
- **(B) D-Galactose** (C2–C5 $\text{OH}$: R, L, L, R) $\to$ *meso*-galactaric (mucic) acid (horizontal plane of symmetry) $\implies$ optically inactive.
- **(C) D-Glucose** (R, L, R, R) and **(D) D-Mannose** (L, L, R, R) lack a symmetry plane $\implies$ optically active aldaric acids.
Hence, **(A) and (B)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about **pyrrole** is/are true?
optionsEn: Its dipole moment points from the nitrogen atom toward the carbon ring (positive end at $\text{N}$, negative end at $\text{C3}-\text{C4}$).
It is a much stronger Brønsted acid ($\text{p}K_a \approx 17.5$) than pyrrolidine ($\text{p}K_a \approx 44$).
It undergoes polymerization in strongly acidic aqueous solutions (such as conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$).
It is much less reactive than benzene toward electrophilic aromatic substitution.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Resonance donation of the $\text{N}$ lone pair into the ring outweighs the $-I$ effect of $\text{N}$, making the $\text{C}$ atoms $\delta-$ and $\text{N}$ $\delta+$.
- **(B) Correct:** Deprotonation of pyrrole gives the aromatic pyrrolide anion (where the newly freed lone pair sits in an $sp^2$ orbital while the $6\,\pi$ sextet remains intact).
- **(C) Correct:** Protonation at C2 destroys aromaticity and generates an electrophilic iminium ion that rapidly polymerizes with neutral pyrrole.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Pyrrole is vastly *more* reactive than benzene toward $\text{S}_\text{E}\text{Ar}$.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements comparing **pyridine** and **benzene** is/are correct?
optionsEn: In pyridine, the lone pair on nitrogen resides in an $sp^2$ hybrid orbital perpendicular to the aromatic $\pi$-cloud.
Pyridine undergoes electrophilic substitution under vigorous conditions predominantly at C3 ($\beta$-position).
Pyridine is more reactive than benzene toward nucleophilic substitution at C2 and C4.
Pyridine undergoes Friedel–Crafts acylation with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ faster than benzene.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** The pyridine $\text{N}$ lone pair is in the plane of the ring ($sp^2$) and does not participate in the $6\,\pi$ sextet.
- **(B) Correct:** Attack at C3 avoids placing positive charge on the electronegative nitrogen atom.
- **(C) Correct:** The ring nitrogen stabilizes negative charge in $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ at C2 and C4.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Pyridine complexes strongly with $\text{AlCl}_3$ (forming a deactivated $N$-acylpyridinium/Lewis adduct) and does not undergo Friedel–Crafts acylation.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of Kekulé resonance structures possible for linear **anthracene** ($\text{C}_{14}\text{H}_{10}$) is _______.
questions.explanationEn: For linear polyacenes with $n$ fused benzene rings, the number of Kekulé structures is $n + 1$. For anthracene ($n = 3$), there are $3 + 1 = \mathbf{4}$ Kekulé resonance structures.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of fused rings in the cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene core of cholesterol is _______.
questions.explanationEn: The cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene skeleton consists of three 6-membered rings (A, B, C) and one 5-membered ring (D), giving **$4$** fused rings.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereogenic (chiral) carbon centers present in a molecule of **cholesterol** is _______.
questions.explanationEn: Cholesterol ($\text{C}_{27}\text{H}_{46}\text{O}$) contains **$8$** stereogenic carbon centers located at positions C3, C8, C9, C10, C13, C14, C17, and C20.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of peptide (amide) bonds present in a linear **pentapeptide** is _______.
questions.explanationEn: A linear polypeptide made of $n$ amino acid residues contains $n - 1$ peptide bonds. For a pentapeptide ($n = 5$), there are $5 - 1 = \mathbf{4}$ peptide bonds.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: Complete oxidative cleavage of $1\text{ mol}$ of D-glucose with excess aqueous $\text{NaIO}_4$ (yielding $5\text{ mol HCO}_2\text{H}$ and $1\text{ mol HCHO}$) consumes _______ moles of $\text{NaIO}_4$.
questions.explanationEn: In D-glucose ($\text{HOCH}_2(\text{CHOH})_4\text{CHO}$), all $5$ carbon–carbon bonds between the $6$ oxygenated carbons are cleaved by periodic acid, consuming **$5$** moles of $\text{NaIO}_4$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry III: Aromatic, Heterocyclic & Natural Products Chemistry (Set 01)
questions.questionTextEn: L-Histidine has $\text{p}K_{a1} = 1.82$ ($\alpha$-carboxyl), $\text{p}K_{aR} = 6.00$ (imidazolium side chain), and $\text{p}K_{a2} = 9.17$ ($\alpha$-ammonium). The isoelectric point ($\text{p}I$) of L-histidine is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
L-Histidine is a basic amino acid: at $\text{pH} < 1.82$ its net charge is $+2$; between $1.82$ and $6.00$ its net charge is $+1$; between $6.00$ and $9.17$ it is neutral ($0$); above $9.17$ it is $-1$. Thus:
$\text{p}I = \frac{6.00 + 9.17}{2} = 7.585 \approx \mathbf{7.59}$.
